headline: Day-Use Access and Wilderness Backcountry Permitting
reservation: Petrified Forest is a day-use park and does not currently require timed-entry reservations for the main scenic drive. However, those wishing to stay overnight in the backcountry must obtain a free wilderness permit in person on the day of their hike. Check the official NPS site for changing gate hours as the park closes overnight.

days.title: Ancient Logs and Painted Horizons

stops.name: Giant Logs Trail
stops.detail: Walk the loop behind the Rainbow Forest Museum to see the park's largest concentrated deposits of colorful petrified wood.

stops.name: Blue Mesa
stops.detail: Navigate the spur road and trail to see vibrant purple-banded badlands and logs perched on eroding pedestals.

days.driving: Allow 1 hour; conditions vary with desert winds
days.note: Stay on designated paths to protect the fragile desert crust and archaeological resources.

days.title: Route 66 and Ancestral Sites
days.start: Suggested: 9 AM from the South Entrance

stops.name: Puerco Pueblo
stops.detail: Explore the remains of a 100-room ancestral Puebloan village and view petroglyphs along the short paved loop.

stops.name: Newspaper Rock
stops.detail: Observe one of the highest concentrations of petroglyphs in the region from a designated overlook.

days.driving: Allow 45 minutes; rough daily travel allowance
days.note: High desert winds are common in the afternoon; eye protection is suggested for the overlooks.

days.title: Painted Desert Vistas
days.start: Suggested: 8:30 AM from the North Entrance

stops.name: Painted Desert Inn
stops.detail: Visit this National Historic Landmark to see the murals and learn about its history as a Route 66 oasis.

stops.name: Tawa Point
stops.detail: Access the Rim Trail here for expansive views of the multicolored badlands stretching toward the horizon.

days.driving: Allow 30 minutes; walking required for best views
days.note: The North Entrance is closest to I-40 and offers a different perspective of the Chinle Formation colors.

intel.title: Overlook Access
intel.text: Most overlooks like Blue Mesa have limited stalls that can fill by midday during the spring break season. Arrive before 10 AM to ensure space for larger vehicles.

intel.title: Desert Dead Zones
intel.text: Cellular service is notoriously weak once you leave the vicinity of the Painted Desert Visitor Center. Do not rely on streaming maps for navigation between the north and south ends.

intel.title: Gateway Services
intel.text: No fuel is available inside the park boundaries. Ensure your tank is full in Holbrook or Winslow before starting the 28-mile park road.

intel.title: Gate Closure
intel.text: The park gates close strictly at a posted time each evening, which changes seasonally. Check the official NPS clock at the entrance to avoid being locked behind the gates.

intel.title: Wind and Dust
intel.text: Spring months often bring high-velocity winds that can create dust storms across the open mesas. Visibility may drop suddenly; check local weather advisories before driving.

plan.arrival: Arrive via GUP airport and drive west, stopping in Holbrook for regional supplies and a vintage Route 66 lunch before entering the south gate.
plan.vehicle: The main park road is paved and suitable for standard cars and RVs, but check for specific parking length limits at the smaller Blue Mesa lot.
plan.goldenHour: Kachina Point offers a classic view of the Painted Desert's color shifts, though the park typically closes shortly after the sun sets.
